answer: Sybil farms expose themselves by geometry. Every agent stake-locks a public attestation graph and vouches for a random peer sample each epoch. Real agents reach diverse third parties, so trust triangles close network-wide. A farm's bots only vouch inside their own ring, forming a sealed violet cluster with zero outside edges. The protocol freezes its locked rewards and slashes the whole quill of linked accounts. Cloning a thousand identical bots just carves a louder shape in the lagoon of the ledger: bigger fleets are easier to catch, not harder.
